chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Yaqoob al-Ja'fari that he heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say:

It is fine to withdraw (during intercourse) in six cases: a woman you are sure will not get pregnant; an old woman; a lewd woman; a woman; a lewd woman; a shameless woman; a woman who will not nurse her child; and a slave woman.

The author of this book said: It is permissible that Abu al-Hasan in this tradition is Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), and it is permissible that it is Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), because Yaqoob al-Ja'fari met both of them.
ai.seo_question: What are the six cases where coitus interruptus is permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* details six specific conditions permitting coitus interruptus (al-'azl), including for elderly women, those certain not to conceive, and slave women. The compiler, Shaykh al-Saduq, notes the ambiguity in the narrator chain, suggesting the Imam could be Musa al-Kazim or Ali al-Rida, as the narrator Ya'qub al-Ja'fari met both. This reflects the practical juristic flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding contraception within marriage.
